result.summary: This is a residential and commercial mixed-use street with narrow sidewalks and parallel parking on both sides. Pedestrian safety is compromised by utility poles obstructing the walkway and a lack of marked crossings or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, significantly reducing the effective width for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates sightline barriers between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs visible on this stretch of the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Obstacle Removal
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles or widen the sidewalk to ensure a clear, accessible path of travel that meets ADA standards.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility continental crosswalk markings at the nearest intersections to clearly define pedestrian space.

result.summary: The image depicts a typical urban residential mid-block environment with a continuous concrete sidewalk and brick row houses. While the walkway is unobstructed, there is a lack of physical buffering between pedestrians and the roadway, and no green infrastructure or pedestrian-scale lighting is visible.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the parking/travel lane, increasing exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground

hazards.name: Sidewalk Surface Cracking
hazards.description: Visible cracks and minor unevenness in the concrete sidewalk present a potential tripping hazard.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with street trees or low-level plantings to provide a physical and psychological buffer from the roadway.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lamps designed to illuminate the walkway specifically, improving safety and visibility during evening hours.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Patch or replace cracked sections of the concrete to ensure a smooth, accessible walking surface.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features continuous sidewalks on both sides, but they lack safety buffers and are obstructed by utility poles. The signalized intersection ahead lacks marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals, creating significant risks for people crossing the street. Road pavement is in poor condition and there is a lack of traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The signalized intersection lacks painted crosswalks, making pedestrian movements less predictable for drivers.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signals are visible at the intersection, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light poles at the intersection

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the path of the sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking width.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a narrow sidewalk in poor condition, characterized by cracking and vegetation growth. Pedestrians lack a buffer from on-street parking, and the environment is devoid of safety features like street lighting or marked crossings.

hazards.name: Uneven Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk pavement is cracked with weeds growing through, creating a trip hazard for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles, particularly the large black SUV, block the view between the sidewalk and the roadway for anyone attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair and level the sidewalk surface to meet accessibility standards and remove tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lamps to provide adequate illumination for the walkway and improve personal security.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.
